feedback: Reinforce that two equally-ticked sides are equal regardless of apparent length.
∠BCA has vertex C, so it is a different angle from ∠ABC (vertex B).
If the learner assumes an unmarked corner is a right angle because it looks square, point out that only a drawn square asserts 90°; unmarked features are unknown.
activities.intendedInsight: Marks are authoritative, three-letter names with different middle letters (vertices) denote different angles (though reversing the outer letters, as in ∠ABC and ∠CBA, names the same angle), and an unmarked feature is not a stated fact.
learnerActions: Answer: 'This side LOOKS longer than that one, but both carry a single tick — which is actually longer?' (Answer: they are equal.)
Show ∠BCA on the same diagram and decide whether it is the same as ∠ABC or a different angle.
Decide what mark to add for a second pair of equal sides so no one confuses it with the first pair (double ticks).
Answer: 'This corner has no square drawn on it — can you be sure it's a right angle? How would the diagram tell you?' (You cannot assume it; unmarked features are unknown.)
activities.title: Probe diagram authority and unmarked features
